+---
+name: Calc (power, lr, delegate)
+lang: javascript
+---
+
+# Calc (power, lr, delegate)
+
+[`calc-pow-lr`](calc-pow-lr.gram.md) with every alternative's action moved out
+to a named delegate (`-> Name`, ADR D48) instead of written inline as
+`{% … %}`. The grammar file now describes structure and precedence only;
+every arithmetic operation lives in one place, `## Externals` (ADR D49), each
+a `### Name` fence spliced verbatim into the generated evaluator. Every
+delegate below has an embedded implementation, so `gramaire emit --backend
+js`'s output runs standalone — no `setExternals` call required (contrast
+[`calc-delegate`](calc-delegate.gram.md)'s `Call`, deliberately left
+unresolved).
+
+This differs from `calc-delegate` in shape, not mechanism: that grammar
+delegates only the alternatives with something genuinely external to reach
+for (`Math.pow`, `toFixed`, a host-supplied function table) and keeps
+ordinary arithmetic inline, on a stratified grammar that needs no precedence
+declarations at all. Here every alternative delegates — including plain
+`+`/`-`/`*`/`/` — on the same ambiguous, precedence-driven shape `calc-pow-lr`
+uses, so the two axes (stratified vs. ambiguous, inline vs. delegated) can be
+told apart cleanly.
+
+`^` (exponentiation) is `%right` and binds tighter than everything else, so
+`2 ^ 3 ^ 2` parses as `2 ^ (3 ^ 2)` (512), not `(2 ^ 3) ^ 2` (64). `%left`
+alone cannot express that. Without a declared precedence for `^` (or any
+operator sharing its production shape), building the LR tables fails outright
+with a shift/reduce conflict — declaring one is a build error to leave
+unresolved, not a warning to ignore.
+
+Unary minus (`Neg`) is the one alternative Bison's original needs `%prec NEG`
+for — a fictitious token giving the `'-' expr` production its own precedence
+level (between `* /` and `^`) distinct from binary `-`'s. Gramaire has no
+`%prec`: ADR D37 defers per-rule precedence overrides, and a production's
+precedence is always its last terminal's, full stop — for `'-' expr` that
+terminal is `'-'` itself, so `Neg` unavoidably inherits `'-'`'s own `%left`
+level rather than sitting on a level of its own. In practice this is harmless
+here: `^` already outranks every other level regardless of where `NEG` would
+go, so `-2 ^ 2` still parses as `-(2 ^ 2)` = `-4`; and a tie between `Neg` and
+a following `+`/`-` resolves the same way `%left` always resolves ties — by
+reducing first — so `-3 - 2` still parses as `(-3) - 2` = `-5`. The only
+divergence from Bison's grouping is `-2 * 3`: `Neg` shifts through `*` instead
+of binding first, producing `-(2 * 3)` rather than `(-2) * 3` — a different
+parse tree, but the identical value (negation distributes over
+multiplication), so the evaluator gives the right answer regardless.
+
+## Tokens
+
+```gramaire
+NUM : /[0-9]+/ ;
+WS  : /[ \t\r\n]+/   -> skip ;
+```
+
+## expr
+
+![Railroad diagram for the expr rule](diagrams-calc-pow-lr-delegate/expr.svg)
+
+<details>
+<summary>Source</summary>
+
+```gramaire
+expr
+  : left:expr '+' right:expr   -> Add
+  | left:expr '-' right:expr   -> Sub
+  | left:expr '*' right:expr   -> Mul
+  | left:expr '/' right:expr   -> Div
+  | left:expr '^' right:expr   -> Pow
+  | '-' expr                   -> Neg
+  | '(' expr ')'               -> Paren
+  | NUM                        -> Lit
+  ;
+```
+
+</details>
+
+## Precedence
+
+```gramaire
+%left '+' '-'
+%left '*' '/'
+%right '^'
+```
+
+## Externals
+
+### Add
+
+```javascript
+(c) => c.left + c.right
+```
+
+### Sub
+
+```javascript
+(c) => c.left - c.right
+```
+
+### Mul
+
+```javascript
+(c) => c.left * c.right
+```
+
+### Div
+
+```javascript
+(c) => c.left / c.right
+```
+
+### Pow
+
+```javascript
+(c) => Math.pow(c.left, c.right)
+```
+
+### Neg
+
+```javascript
+(c) => -c.expr
+```
+
+### Paren
+
+```javascript
+(c) => c.expr
+```
+
+### Lit
+
+```javascript
+(c) => Number(c.num)
+```
+
+## Error messages
+
+```text
+after a complete expression, lookahead is NUM:
+  Two values in a row — an operator (`+ - * / ^`) is missing between them.
+```
+
+## Generated tables
+
+<!-- Generated by Gramaire — do not edit; run `gramaire fmt` to refresh. -->
+
+| Nonterminal | FIRST                | FOLLOW                                                          |
+| ----------- | -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
+| `expr`      | `left` `-` `(` `NUM` | `+` `Add` `-` `Sub` `*` `Mul` `/` `Div` `^` `Pow` `Neg` `)` `$` |

+name: Calc (power)

+
+# Calc (power)
+
+The [`calc-prec`](calc-prec.gram.md) shape — `expr op expr` for every operator,
+ambiguity resolved entirely by `## Precedence` (ADR D37) — extended to a real,
+working evaluator: this is GNU Bison's own "Infix Notation Calculator"
+tutorial grammar, translated one alternative at a time. Each action computes
+an actual number (`c.left + c.right`), the same way Bison's `$$ = $1 + $3`
+does, rather than building a tagged AST node.
+
+`^` (exponentiation) is `%right` and binds tighter than everything else, so
+`2 ^ 3 ^ 2` parses as `2 ^ (3 ^ 2)` (512), not `(2 ^ 3) ^ 2` (64). `%left`
+alone cannot express that. Without a declared precedence for `^` (or any
+operator sharing its production shape), building the LR tables fails outright
+with a shift/reduce conflict — declaring one is a build error to leave
+unresolved, not a warning to ignore.
+
+Unary minus (`Neg`) is the one alternative Bison's original needs `%prec NEG`
+for — a fictitious token giving the `'-' expr` production its own precedence
+level (between `* /` and `^`) distinct from binary `-`'s. Gramaire has no
+`%prec`: ADR D37 defers per-rule precedence overrides, and a production's
+precedence is always its last terminal's, full stop — for `'-' expr` that
+terminal is `'-'` itself, so `Neg` unavoidably inherits `'-'`'s own `%left`
+level rather than sitting on a level of its own. In practice this is harmless
+here: `^` already outranks every other level regardless of where `NEG` would
+go, so `-2 ^ 2` still parses as `-(2 ^ 2)` = `-4`; and a tie between `Neg` and

+```gramaire
+NUM : /[0-9]+/ ;
+WS  : /[ \t\r\n]+/   -> skip ;
+```
+
+## expr
+
+![Railroad diagram for the expr rule](diagrams-calc-pow-lr/expr.svg)
+
+<details>
+<summary>Source</summary>
+
+```gramaire

+  | left:expr '-' right:expr   {% (c) => c.left - c.right %}
+  | left:expr '*' right:expr   {% (c) => c.left * c.right %}
+  | left:expr '/' right:expr   {% (c) => c.left / c.right %}
+  | left:expr '^' right:expr   {% (c) => Math.pow(c.left, c.right) %}
+  | '-' expr                   {% (c) => -c.expr %}
+  | '(' expr ')'               {% (c) => c.expr %}
+  | NUM                        {% (c) => Number(c.num) %}
+  ;
+```
+
+</details>
+
+## Precedence
+
+```gramaire
+%left '+' '-'
+%left '*' '/'
+%right '^'
+```
+

+```text
+after a complete expression, lookahead is NUM:
+  Two values in a row — an operator (`+ - * / ^`) is missing between them.
+```
